subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should this issue be resolved by documenting HTTP Request URLs as the preferred low-latency hosted Slack transport, or should OpenClaw change Slack setup/default behavior beyond the existing `mode: "http"` support?
rationale: HTTP mode already exists and the remaining measured delay is mostly outside OpenClaw code, but stronger steering or default changes affect Slack setup expectations, public ingress requirements, and operator guidance.

options.title: Document HTTP Latency Guidance
options.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local/private deployments and explicitly recommend HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress Slack deployments where reply latency matters.

options.title: Change Setup Or Defaults
options.body: Sponsor a stronger setup/default change that steers new hosted Slack installs away from Socket Mode, with upgrade and operator guidance.

options.title: Accept Current Guidance
options.body: Decide the existing transport table is sufficient and close later with a maintainer note that no additional latency-specific guidance is planned.

recommendation.title: Document HTTP Latency Guidance
recommendation.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default for local/private deployments and explicitly recommend HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress Slack deployments where reply latency matters.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the measurement, merged the current-main partial fix, and scoped the remaining follow-up to HTTP mode guidance.
